transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... I just can't seem to shake this feeling that I've failed. I feel like I've failed as a father, and just as a useful person in general. The thought just keeps looping in my head, over and over. It gets to the point where I start to feel like I really don't deserve much of a future.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It's been... I'd say about a month now. It started right around the time my daughter left for college. She moved out of state for school, and... yeah, it's just been going on ever since then.
Have you been enjoying activities or hobbies that you normally like to do over the past month?

No, not at all. I used to really look forward to working on my model railway, and... watching the Cubs games with my daughter. But now, the trains just sit there half-built on the table. I haven't touched them. And even just turning on a game on TV feels completely pointless. I just don't have the interest anymore.
Have you experienced any pleasure in things over the past month?
No, honestly, I haven't. There's just... no joy in anything right now. It all just feels flat.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or how you've been moving around over the past month?

Yeah, my energy is... it's pretty much zero. It really doesn't matter how long I've been in bed or how much I try to rest. Even simple things, like... carrying a basket of laundry upstairs, or even just standing there sorting the mail... it feels like I'm moving through wet cement. Everything just takes so much effort now.
Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself over the past month?

Yeah. I've been having thoughts that... it would just be easier if I didn't wake up. It actually scared me a little bit recently because I caught myself going over all my finances. I was looking through everything, almost like I was getting things ready for someone else to take over. So... yeah, I have.
Have you experienced any strange or unusual thoughts, like hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there, over the past month?
No, nothing like that. I haven't heard any voices or seen anything that isn't there. It's just... the depression, I guess. But no strange thoughts like that.
Has your depression worsened at any point over the past month, or has it stayed about the same?

I'd say it's stayed about the same. I haven't really noticed a specific point where it suddenly got worse... it's just been consistently bad this entire month. Every day is pretty much the same heavy feeling.
Have you ever felt this way before, like you're experiencing now, in the past?
No, I... I don't think so. I've never really felt like this before. This is... it's all new to me, this kind of heavy feeling. I haven't gone through anything like this in the past.
Have you had more than one episode of depression in your lifetime?
No, like I just said, I haven't ever felt this way before. This is the first time I've dealt with anything like this. So, no, just this one time.
Is the lack of pleasure in activities something that happens all the time, or are there moments where you feel slightly better about things?

It's pretty much all the time. I don't really have moments where I feel better or enjoy things anymore. I used to really look forward to working on my model railway, or watching Cubs games with my daughter. But now... the trains just sit half-built on the table. And even just putting a game on the TV feels completely pointless. I just don't get anything out of it right now.
How much of the day do you spend thinking about these feelings of failure?

Honestly, it's most of the day. It just... it keeps looping in my head. That's actually why I came in, because I just can't shake this feeling that I've completely failed. Failed as a father, and just failed at being a useful person in general. It just plays over and over until I... I start to feel like I don't even deserve much of a future.
Have you experienced any significant weight loss or gain over the past month?

Yeah, I've definitely lost some weight. I've had to tighten my belt a notch or two recently. Most days I just... I don't bother making a real meal anymore. I usually just forget to eat until it's late in the day, and even then, I only really manage to get down some toast or a bowl of cereal.
Would you say your depression is interfering with your daily life a lot or just somewhat?

I'd say it's interfering a lot. My bills and house projects are just... they're piling up right now because I can't seem to make myself follow through on anything. And I've completely stopped seeing the few people I used to count on, like the guys at my book club or when we'd go out on rides. I just don't go anymore. 

Honestly, I don't feel safe just brushing this off as a slump anymore. Especially after I caught myself organizing my finances recently... putting all my accounts in order like someone else might need to take them over soon. So, yeah, it's definitely a lot.
Would you say your feelings of failure and low energy are keeping you from doing most things, most of the time?

Yeah, exactly. Like I was just saying, it really is most things, most of the time. I just don't have the energy to follow through on anything, which is why those bills and house projects are just sitting there piling up. And I've totally stopped socializing with the guys from my book club or going on rides. It's affecting every part of my day. 

Like I mentioned, catching myself organizing my accounts so someone else could take them over... that was a wake-up call. I can't just brush this off anymore. So, yes, it's keeping me from doing almost everything.
Have you had any periods in your life where you felt completely better from these kinds of feelings for at least a couple of months?

No, not really. I mean... maybe I've had a day or two here and there where things didn't feel quite as heavy, but a whole couple of months? No. It's just been this same low feeling for a long time now. I honestly can't remember the last time I felt completely normal for that long of a stretch.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months where you didn't feel depressed?
Like I just said, no, I haven't. It hasn't let up for a full two months. Just a day or two of feeling okay, maybe, but that's it. It's been pretty constant.
Have you had any previous episodes of depression that lasted for less than two months?

No, not really. I... I don't think I've ever had short spells of it, if that's what you mean. It hasn't been something that comes and goes quickly. It's really just been this one long, continuous stretch of feeling this way.
Have you had an episode of depression like this before that lasted for more than two months and then completely went away?

No, I haven't. I... I feel like we keep circling back to this, but no. It's never gone away completely. I haven't had a past time where I felt this low and then just got better. It really has just been this current, ongoing stretch.
